features.name: Roman public buildings in fiefs (18 improvement types, upkeep, effects)
features.summary: Replaces Native's 6 village/castle improvements with 25 building slots: village works (manor, mill, watch tower, school, messenger post, prison tower, plantation, lumber yard) and town/castle buildings (mercenary hall, merchant guild, military academy, forge, arsenal, stables, training ground, shooting range) plus Roman-only monuments (horreum, thermae, templum, castra, basilica, aquaeductus, amphitheatrum). Each has a cost, build time, a monthly effect, and the Roman monuments charge the player a monthly upkeep.
features.mechanics: Player picks a building in menu:center_manage (one option per building, gated by settlement type, existing slot, nearby-school for the academy, cf_center_is_roman for slots 148-154) -> menu:center_improve (lumber yard slot 134 lowers cost) -> improve_center stores the type in party slot 124 and finish-hour in 125 -> strig:69 (and a duplicate strig:112) every 12h sets party slot <type>=1 and logs 'Building of X finished'. Effects: strig:82 (every 720h) calls center_apply_monthly_building_effects (prosperity +1..+3 for plantation 133, merchant guild 139, forge 141, horreum 148, basilica 152, aquaeductus 153, +1 if romanitas>=50; garrison XP via party_upgrade_with_xp for training ground 144/shooting range 145/castra 151; castra adds 3-6 faction tier-2 troops; templum 150/thermae 149/amphitheatrum 154 add +1 village relation slot 26) and then charges upkeep 200-600 denars per monument from the player, or drops relation by 2 if unpaid. Other readers: strig:44 weekly rent +20% basilica / +10% merchant guild (party slot 47); update_mercenary_units_of_towns (mercenary hall 138: better and +4 mercenaries); refresh_center_stables (stables 143: extra horse merchandise); center_get_food_consumption (horreum: -40% food use); update_volunteer_troops_in_village (horreum x1.5 volunteers, templum better tier); enter_court (castra +2, arsenal +1 hall guards); get_center_ideal_prosperity (mill 146).
evidence: dis bi get_improvement_details: 25 named buildings with costs (Manor 8000 ... Amphitheatrum 24000)
slot bi party 148/153: written only by menu:center_manage options, read by monthly effects/food/recruit scripts
dis bi strig:82: upkeep + 'You cannot pay for the upkeep of the public buildings in {s4}. They fall into disrepair.'
dis bi strig:69: completion sets party slot <type>=1

features.name: Garrison combat bonuses from fief buildings
features.summary: Soldiers fighting for a settlement (its garrison) get damage and speed bonuses from that settlement's buildings, and an arsenal refills their ammunition during the battle.
features.mechanics: ti_on_agent_spawn trigger in every field/siege mission template (e.g. mst:lead_charge/t5): if agent_get_party_id is a center (35..456), damage modifier +10% castra(151) +5% training ground(144) +5% templum(150); speed modifier +5% thermae(149) +5% amphitheatrum(154). features.name: Romanitas (how Roman a settlement is)
features.summary: Each settlement has a 0-100 'Romanitas' score built from its Roman monuments plus +25 if it belongs to a Roman faction. High Romanitas makes the settlement more prosperous, its people friendlier, its volunteers better, and its townsfolk more willing to fight under siege.
features.mechanics: center_recalculate_romanitas (called monthly from center_apply_monthly_building_effects, strig:82) sums horreum 5, castra 5, templum 8, thermae 12, basilica 12, aquaeductus 15, amphitheatrum 18, +25 Roman faction, caps at 100, stores in party slot 605. Readers: monthly effects (+1 prosperity at >=50, +1 relation at >=70), update_volunteer_troops_in_village (>=50: +2 upgrade rolls, +15% chance -> higher-tier volunteers), process_sieges (romanitas/10 added to siege militia size).
evidence: dis bi center_recalculate_romanitas
slot bi party 605: written only by center_recalculate_romanitas; read by process_sieges and update_volunteer_troops_in_village
dis bi cf_center_is_roman: faction ids map to fac_kingdom_1 Rome, 7 Roman Gallia, 8 Roman Illyricum, 9 Roman Asia, 10 Roman Hispania (factions.txt)

features.name: Townsfolk take up arms when a town is besieged
features.summary: When an enemy army starts besieging a town or castle, a one-time levy of armed townsmen joins the garrison, sized by the town's prosperity and Romanitas (up to 30). The player gets a message for their own fiefs.
features.mechanics: Inside Native's process_sieges loop (BI adds ~19 statements), when a besieger is found: if party slot 616 is 0 and the center is not a village, adds (prosperity/8 + romanitas/10, max 30) trp_townsman to the center, sets slot 616=1 and, for player-owned centers, logs '{reg4} townsfolk of {s4} take up arms.'. lift_siege resets slot 616 to 0 so the levy can happen again next siege.
evidence: dis bi process_sieges @56-75
slot bi party 616: process_sieges e1/s1, lift_siege s1

features.name: Military academy: pay to upgrade troops in a town
features.summary: In your own kingdom's towns with a military academy, a town-menu option opens a screen where you can pay the normal join cost to upgrade soldiers in your party to either of their next troop types, limited by the academy's remaining capacity.
features.mechanics: menu:town option town_upgrade (needs party slot 140 >= 1, town of player's kingdom, player or kingdom-owned) shows the capacity and starts prsnt:upgrade_troops. The presentation lists party stacks; picking upgrade path 0/1 (troop_get_upgrade_troop) multiplies game_get_join_cost by count, removes gold, swaps troops (party_remove_members/party_add_members) and writes the reduced capacity back to party slot 140. Building the academy (menu:center_manage center_build_academy) requires a village of that town to have a school (slot 135).

features.name: AI lords build improvements in their fiefs
features.summary: AI lords spend their personal wealth to construct buildings in the fiefs they own, so NPC territory develops over time like the player's. Fiefs also start the game with buildings allocated from a wealth budget.
features.mechanics: Native troop_does_business_in_center (lord visits his fief) now calls npc_upgrade_buildings(lord, center): wealth threshold depends on lord reputation type (troop slot 52); if lord wealth (troop slot 11) exceeds it and nothing is under construction (party slot 124), picks a random free building slot 130-154 (towns: 137+, Roman-only 148+ via cf_center_is_roman), computes build days from cost, lord engineer skill x intelligence, level and the center's prosperity, deducts the cost and calls improve_center. Player is told '{s10} constructs a {s0} in {s4}, finish in {reg0} days' for lords of their kingdom. game_start calls allocate_buildings to seed buildings.
evidence: explain bi npc_upgrade_buildings: caller troop_does_business_in_center, displayed text '{s10}_constructs_a_{s0}_in_{s4},_finish_in_{reg0}_days'
dis bi npc_upgrade_buildings (random slot 130-155, cost/time formula)
explain bi allocate_buildings: caller game_start, text '{s51} allocated {reg0} wealth for buildings'

features.name: Triumphus after taking a city
features.summary: A vassal of a Roman faction with 150+ renown who captures a town (not castles: the gate is center id 35-99, BI's town range) and is on good terms (+10) with the emperor may be granted a triumph: a celebratory screen offering a parade through the city for +25 renown, +3 relation with the ruler and a cash share of the spoils (25 x the captured fief's prosperity, 500-2525 denars). It can be refused.
features.mechanics: menu:castle_taken calls cf_player_deserves_triumphus(center): center is a town (ids 35-99), player has homage, player kingdom is one of the Roman factions, troop slot 7 (renown) >= 150, ruler (faction slot 11) relation >= 10 -> jump_to_menu 77 (menu_triumphus, bare integer). menu_triumphus computes spoils from party slot 50 (prosperity) into $g_triumphus_spoils; accept option calls change_troop_renown 25, change_player_relation_with_troop ruler 3, troop_add_gold.
evidence: grep bi: menu:castle_taken @27 (jump_to_menu, 77) after cf_player_deserves_triumphus call
dis bi menu:triumphus + opt triumphus_accept conseq
menu text 'The senate and people of {s10} have decreed a triumphus...'

features.name: Battle morale recalculation spread over three ticks (performance)
features.summary: Native's every-3-seconds morale pass compares every soldier with every other soldier, which lags big battles. BI processes only a third of the soldiers each pass, cutting that cost to a third.
features.mechanics: apply_effect_of_other_people_on_courage_scores (called from mst:lead_charge/t19 every 3s) cycles $courage_update_phase 0-2 and only updates agents whose id mod 3 equals the phase; the inner all-agents loop is unchanged.
evidence: dis bi apply_effect_of_other_people_on_courage_scores @0-8
global bi courage_update_phase: sole writer/reader is that script
